subject: known_incompatibilities: '' vs NULL distinct
decision: no nullable text column in schema billing (every text column is NOT NULL); the only nullable columns are subscriptions.ends_on / suspended_on (date), mapped with null_missing_equiv. No decision needed.

subject: known_incompatibilities: timestamp precision (us -> ms)
decision: timestamptz columns occurred_at, created_at, issued_at, sent_at. Every runtime write is a date cast (p_period_end::timestamptz, p_as_of::timestamptz) and seeded values are whole seconds, so no microsecond information exists; canon rule datetime_utc_truncate_ms applies to both sides under tol-v1.

subject: known_incompatibilities: session TimeZone affects timestamptz
decision: pin the source session to UTC (SET TIME ZONE 'UTC') in the loader and in recon; occurred_at::date BETWEEN ... in rating.sql:46 / 90 is evaluated in session time, so the app-side range is [periodStart 00:00Z, periodEnd+1d 00:00Z). BSON date is UTC.

subject: known_incompatibilities: identity / serial sequences
decision: none: census.sequences = [] and every primary key is uuid. Seeded rows carry fixed uuids; procedure-created rows carry md5(...)::uuid identifiers (rating.sql:103,127; invoicing.sql:85-86,109; dunning.sql:46; plans.sql:60; dunning.sql:77). _id strategy: the source uuid survives the load as _id (BSON binData subtype 4) on every collection and as the element `id` inside creditNotes / invoiceLines / dunningAttempts / rating, so the parity transcripts line up; the app keeps computing the same md5 identifiers until cutover (new documents may switch to ObjectId after cutover).

subject: known_incompatibilities: partitioned / inherited tables
decision: none: census tables[*].partitioned = false for all 11 tables.

subject: known_incompatibilities: identifier case folding
decision: all identifiers are unquoted lower_snake_case in schema.sql; targets are camelCase per the proposer; no quoted identifiers.

subject: known_incompatibilities: deferrable constraints
decision: none in schema.sql (no DEFERRABLE clause).

subject: known_incompatibilities: partial / expression indexes
decision: none: the 22 catalog indexes are primary-key and UNIQUE btree indexes without predicates (census.indexes).

subject: known_incompatibilities: NULL elements in arrays
decision: no array-typed columns in schema billing; target arrays (creditNotes, invoiceLines, dunningAttempts) are built from rows and cannot hold null elements.

subject: known_incompatibilities: collation order
decision: text ORDER BY in fn_list_plans (code), fn_usage_summary (kind), sp_issue_invoice credit FIFO (issued_on, id): plan codes are upper-case ASCII, kinds lower-case ASCII, so libc order equals MongoDB binary order on this data; uuid order (id) must be compared as binData bytes, same as PostgreSQL uuid order.

subject: known_incompatibilities: PL/pgSQL routines
decision: 12 routines, no triggers (census.triggers = []); each is dispositioned `migrate` in NOTES.md s2.3 and its conversion pattern is recorded per routine in the plsql_unit_needs_manual_review resolutions below (p4 conversion_patterns input).

subject: known_incompatibilities: row-level security
decision: none: billing_ro sees every row of every table (NOTES.md s2.3 access check; row counts equal seed.sql INSERT rows).

subject: known_incompatibilities: materialized views
decision: none: census.views = [] and census.materialized_views = [].

subject: known_incompatibilities: ON CONFLICT upserts
decision: four sites become idempotent updateOne(upsert): rating_periods ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, period_start) DO UPDATE period_end (rating.sql:117) -> updateOne ratingPeriods {tenantId, periodStart} upsert; rating_results ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE (133) -> same updateOne, $set only used/rollover/billable/overage, $setOnInsert the rest; invoices ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE status (invoicing.sql:100) -> updateOne invoices {_id} upsert with $setOnInsert tenantId/periodId/issuedAt and $set status; dunning_attempts ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (dunning.sql:48) -> updateOne invoices {_id, 'dunningAttempts.attemptNo': {$ne}} $push; notifications WHERE NOT EXISTS (dunning.sql:79-84) -> updateOne {tenantId, kind, sentAt} upsert $setOnInsert.

subject: money columns
decision: numeric(12,2) (monthly_fee, amounts, subtotal/tax/total, overage_amount) and numeric(12,6) (overage_rate) load as Decimal128 with the source scale, never double or minor-unit integers; tol-v1 numeric_abs_tol 0 so the loader must not re-round. PostgreSQL round(numeric, 2) is half-away-from-zero: the p4 app-side rating/invoice arithmetic must use Decimal with ROUND_HALF_UP semantics to reproduce rating.sql:60 and invoicing.sql:115-124.

evidence.quote: v_total := round(v_subtotal + v_tax - v_credit, 2);

subject: fixture coverage gaps (s2.4 manifest)
decision: (1) rating_periods->usage_events has no FK and no event falls in any seeded period: the model keeps the legacy join as a range query on usageEvents (tenantId, occurredAt), so an empty period rates to used_units 0 exactly as fn_usage_rating does. (2) invoices.period_id crosses tenants (invoices of tenants Two/Five/Six point at tenant One's periods): invoices and ratingPeriods are both top-level collections referencing tenants and each other by _id, so the cross-tenant shape loads as-is with no tenant constraint on periodId; nothing is embedded under tenants that would need the period. (3) Threshold / 16 MB behaviour is not exercised at 49 rows; the only unbounded child (usage_events) is a collection, every embed is bounded by construction or cadence (1:1 rating; exactly 5 lines per invoice; one dunning attempt per schedule run while overdue, ~22 KB after a year of daily runs; per-tenant credit notes with no insert path).

Pure read.

migrate (NOTES.md s2.3): read: usageEvents aggregate $match {tenantId, occurredAt range} $group by kind {count, sum units} $sort kind.

migrate (NOTES.md s2.3): write: subscriptions.updateMany({tenantId, endsOn: null, startsOn < effectiveOn}, set endsOn = effectiveOn-1 and status active unless cancelled) then insertOne({_id: md5(tenant||plan||effective_on), tenantId, planId, startsOn, status active}); two statements on one collection -> one multi-document transaction.

migrate (NOTES.md s2.3): write: fn_usage_rating then a single updateOne(upsert) on ratingPeriods {tenantId, periodStart}: $set periodEnd (ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, period_start) DO UPDATE period_end), $setOnInsert _id = md5(tenant||period_start), rating.id = md5(period_id), rating.subscriptionId, rating.quotaUnits, rating.createdAt = periodEnd 00:00Z (the rating_results INSERT columns the ON CONFLICT (id) clause does not touch), $set rating.usedUnits, rating.rolloverUnits = max(quota-used,0), rating.billableUnits, rating.overageAmount (the four columns rating.sql:133-137 updates). Re-finalizing a period therefore keeps the original subscription, quota and createdAt exactly as the source does.

migrate (NOTES.md s2.3): write: sp_finalize_rating; updateOne(upsert) invoices {_id: md5(period_id||'invoice')}: $setOnInsert tenantId, periodId, issuedAt = periodEnd 00:00Z (INSERT columns), $set status = 'issued' only (invoicing.sql:100 ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET status), so a reissue keeps the original issuedAt; invoiceLines replaced wholesale from fn_invoice_preview (DELETE+INSERT -> $set array), totals rounded to 2 places; then FIFO credit application as updateOne on tenants with arrayFilters per creditNotes.id ordered by issuedOn, id. Touches ratingPeriods, invoices, tenants -> one multi-document transaction.

migrate (NOTES.md s2.3): write: for each invoices.find({status: 'overdue'}).sort({issuedAt, _id}): attemptNo = max(dunningAttempts.attemptNo)+1, scheduledFor = asOf rolled off the weekend, updateOne({_id, 'dunningAttempts.attemptNo': {$ne: attemptNo}}, {$push: {dunningAttempts: {id: md5(invoice_id||attempt_no), tenantId, attemptNo, scheduledFor, status scheduled}}}) — idempotent like ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING.

migrate (NOTES.md s2.3): write: for each distinct tenantId of invoices {status overdue, issuedAt < (asOf - 13d) 00:00Z} (issued_at::date <= p_as_of - 14 as an exclusive start-of-next-day bound, so an invoice issued at 09:00 on the cutoff day still qualifies) whose tenant is active: tenants.updateOne status suspended; subscriptions.updateMany({tenantId, status active}, set status suspended, suspendedOn asOf); notifications.updateOne({tenantId, kind suspension, sentAt asOf 00:00Z}, $setOnInsert {_id: md5(tenant||'suspension'||as_of)}, upsert). Three collections -> one multi-document transaction.
